data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jeroboam total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: ירבעם
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ירבעם מורכב משתי מילים עבריות: 'ריב' או 'גדול' ו'עם'. הוא מתייחס לאדם שגדל את העם או שיש לו ריב עם האל או עם העם. בהקשר המקראי, ירבעם היה מלך ישראל הראשון אחרי פילוג הממלכה.

in_greek.name: Ιεροβοάμ
in_greek.meaning: Ο λαός πολλαπλασιάζεται ή Ο λαός είναι μέγας
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ιεροβοάμ προέρχεται από τις εβραϊκές λέξεις 'ריב' (rīb) ή 'גדול' (gadol) και 'עם' (ʿām). Ο Ιεροβοάμ ήταν ο πρώτος βασιλιάς του Βασιλείου του Ισραήλ μετά τη διάσπαση της ενωμένης μοναρχίας Ισραήλ και Ιούδα.

in_latin.name: Jeroboam
in_latin.meaning: The people are many or The people are great
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Jeroboam comes from the Hebrew words 'ריב' (rīb) or 'גדול' (gadol) and 'עם' (ʿām). Jeroboam was the first king of the Kingdom of Israel after the division of the united monarchy of Israel and Judah. He is known for leading the Israelites into idolatry.

in_english.name: Jeroboam
in_english.meaning: The people are many or great
in_english.long_meaning: The name Jeroboam originates from the Hebrew words 'יריב' (yārīb) meaning 'to contend' or 'גדול' (gadol) meaning 'great' and 'עם' (ʿām) meaning 'people'. In the biblical context, Jeroboam I was the first king of the northern Kingdom of Israel, ruling from around 930 to 909 BCE. He is infamous for introducing golden calf idolatry, leading the Israelites away from worshiping Yahweh.

data.cultural_impact: Jeroboam is remembered in history as a king who led Israel into a period of political and religious division. After Solomon’s death, Jeroboam led the Israelites in the north to break away from the southern kingdom of Judah and establish their own independent kingdom. He is also known for leading the Israelites into the worship of golden calves as idolatrous alternatives to Yahweh (1 Kings 12). This legacy has made the name Jeroboam synonymous with rebellion, division, and apostasy in Jewish and Christian tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: Jeroboam's name, meaning 'God will exalt,' might be a reminder of the irony of human ambition and how it can lead to the exact opposite of what we intend. God can use even the most rebellious hearts to bring about His purposes, but the path that Jeroboam chose led to a spiritual Wilderness. Jeroboam's story can serve as a cautionary tale, encouraging us to examine our motivations and to trust in God's plan for our lives, even when it may seem counterintuitive or unpromising.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jeroboam: House of Baal. In the Old Testament, Jeroboam led the northern kingdom of Israel away from God, establishing idolatrous shrines and worshiping false gods. This name is a reminder of the destructive power of turning away from the divine.

biblical_reference.note: Jeroboam I was a major figure in the history of Israel, leading the northern tribes in rebellion against Rehoboam, the son of Solomon.

historical_references.reference: Jeroboam was the first king of the northern kingdom of Israel, son of Nebat, who rebelled against Rehoboam, Solomon's successor. He established the political and religious center at Shechem and Dan.
historical_references.context: After Solomon's death, ten of the twelve tribes of Israel rebelled against Rehoboam and chose Jeroboam as their king.

historical_references.reference: Jeroboam II is considered the greatest king of the northern kingdom of Israel, ruling around 793-753 BC. His military campaigns expanded Israel's territory to reach roughly the borders of the kingdom of Solomon.
historical_references.context: Jeroboam II succeeded Zechariah and restored Israel's power and prosperity, defeating the Arameans and Syrians.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Jeroboam is most commonly associated with an ancient king of the Northern Kingdom of Israel in the Bible. However, in modern context, his name is also seen on various platforms. In movies and TV shows, Jeroboam has been depicted in several productions such as the 1993 miniseries 'Shalom Sesame' and the 2014 movie 'Exodus: Gods and Kings'. In literature and poetry, Jeroboam is referenced in works such as Charles Dickens' 'Barnaby Rudge' and William Shakespeare's 'King Lear'. In news and current events, the name Jeroboam is often used metaphorically to refer to political and religious controversies, such as the ongoing debates surrounding the separation of church and state in the United States.
